newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek shares firm 1.92pct towards historic high.
newsitem.headline: Greek shares firm 1.92pct towards historic high.

text.p: Greek shares resumed their climb after Friday's mild correction and the general index got closer to its all-time high helped by industrials, banks and construction.

The Athens general index firmed 1.92 percent or 31.44 points to 1,670.23 from Friday's 1,638.79 close, reaching an intra-day and year high of 1,669.61, some 15 points short of the all-time high of 1,684.31 set in August 1990.
Market participants said the rally had considerable underlying support because retail investors continued to focus on blue chips and re-invest their profits.

"The on-going rally has considerable underlying support. Investors avoid speculative stocks, focusing on blue chips and medium-sized companies with good prospects which ensure their returns and re-investment of profits," said Michael Eleftheriou, fund manager at Alpha Mutual Funds.
He said improved macroeconomic conditions attracted new funds which supported prices amidst profit-taking.
"The macroeconomic environment ensures that the rise is sustainable as opposed to speculative moves with little fundamental justification observed in past years," Eleftheriou said.
Absorption of profit-taking is superb, giving rise to short-lived price correction patterns, he added.
Foreign investors are seeing reducing their equity exposure while domestic institutionals were ploughing back profits.
"Foreign institutionals are mostly on the sell side and their orders are executed comfortably in a high-volume environment," said Eleftheriou.
Domestic institutionals follow the market, continuously rebalancing their portfolios as profits are ploughed back, he added.
Turnover reached a satisfactory 30.2 billion drachmas in volume of 7.2 million shares.

Block trading was very active, including Attica Enterprises, 100,000 shares at 5,520 drachmas, Hellenic Bottling, 20,000 shares at 11,550, Alpha Credit Bank, 35,000 shares at 21,290, and, 3,000 shares at 34,700.
Blocks were also traded in Macedonia-Thrace Bank, Titan Cement, National Bank, Ionian Bank, Metrolife, Delta Dairy preferred, Sarantis and Hellenic Biscuits.
Advancers led decliners 160 to 80 with 17 stocks unchanged on 257 traded.
The Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 3,800 drachmas was quoted higher at 1,096-1,126. Shares of OTE telecom, the underlying, firmed 45 drachmas to 6,550.
The Merrill Lynch American call warrant on a basket of 23 Greek equities that are part of the Athens general index was quoted higher at 702.71-747.56. The warrants expire January 9 1998.

The ING Baring Financial Products American style call warrant based on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted higher at $90.81-$92.51. The strike price is set at $99.60 and the warrants expire October 8, 1997.

The ING Baring Financial Products American-style call warrant on a basket of six blue-chips denominated in drachmas was quoted higher at 3,757-3,983 drachmas. The strike price is set at 10,000 drachmas and the warrants expire on February 2, 1998.
The ING Baring American-style second call warrant on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted higher at $23.11-N/O. The strike price is set at $110.0 and the warrants expire April 9 1998.

The recently launched ING Baring American-style, drachma- denominated call warrant on the bourse's benchmark index was quoted higher at 299-332 drachmas. The strike price is set at 1,639 points and the warrants expire May 14 1998. --Angelos Kiosklis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4 (c) Reuters Limited 1997
